A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same capability-localization study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-model head-ablation experiments, method comparisons, capability generalization and universal-head analyses, with detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports additional larger-model evaluations, ProxySPEX comparisons, stability analyses and ablation controls.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equation 1 retain the same Bernoulli/stratified knockout measurements, Lasso regression and selection of heads with the most negative coefficients. Universal-head filtering also remains. Additional implementation explanations and alternative-ablation experiments do not establish a revised identification method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K/Arithmetic, MBPP/HumanEval, custom swearing and rhyming tasks, general-language benchmarks and WMDP subdomains. No additional dataset or task coverage is established; Qwen 2.5 14B extends model configurations.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated, closely related sparse-recovery comparator, ProxySPEX, in Section 6.4/Table 8, and a random-five-head control in Appendix B.2/Table 10. These substantially strengthen the comparison set beyond the retained greedy, one-shot greedy and Bernoulli compressed-sensing comparisons in Table 4.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen 2.5 14B evaluation, 100/200/300-mask stability experiments, Recall@2/5/10 and mean/random-ablation controls. The new ProxySPEX comparison uses 500 evaluations over layers 14–16, comprising 96 heads, versus whole-model searches over 1,024 heads for the proposed method. The original subset-identification/full-dataset evaluation procedure remains.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained head-count and WMDP analyses, v2 adds mask-budget sensitivity and head-recovery stability tests, zero-versus-mean ablation, random-head controls and universal-head attention-pattern analysis. The introduction also reports preliminary experiments showing poor performance when only task-specific heads are retained, directly probing sufficiency.

E5.justification: v1 does not report repeated-run uncertainty. v2 introduces three-seed means and standard deviations for central results, seed-averaged recall and uncertainty in detailed appendix tables; Appendix B.1 specifies four dataset-subsampling seeds for its ablation comparison. This establishes expanded reporting, not an increase from a known v1 run count.

E6.justification: Central reported summaries change: Table 2's Llama 3.1 8B GSM8K drop changes from -48.4 to -40.6 ± 6.8, and Qwen 7B's from -65.4 to -60.5 ± 4.4. Figure 1 also updates. New results cover Qwen 14B, Qwen universal heads, stability, ProxySPEX and ablation controls. Table 4 and the original appendix head lists remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The head-importance definitions, sparse linear formulation, Lasso objective and compressed-sensing measurement argument remain unchanged. The added explanation limiting approximate additivity to task-specific heads clarifies the existing assumption; no new formal result, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the central claim from capabilities being implemented or highly localized in sparse components to critically depending on those components. The introduction explicitly states that the identified heads are necessary but insufficient and do not form self-contained circuits. The reported validation range also expands from 1–8B to 1–14B.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limits on sufficiency and linearity, explains low recovery recall through a smaller effective set of critical heads and noisy selections, and discusses the accuracy–evaluation-budget tradeoff. It also adds a tentative attention-sink interpretation for L0H31 and connects recovered arithmetic heads to previously described operand-processing mechanisms.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents a step-by-step workflow, per-model/task mask counts and sparsities, scikit-learn Lasso settings including alpha=0.01 and max_iter=5000, jointly fitted intercepts, custom-task subsample sizes and all 12 swearing prompts. These materially improve reproducibility without establishing changes to previously unspecified settings. Resource-access links remain equivalent.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantial positioning within feature attribution and circuit discovery, including SPEX, ProxySPEX, SHAP/LIME, gradient attribution and causal interventions. Section 6.4 explicitly distinguishes efficient first-order head identification from interaction reconstruction, while new mechanistic discussion connects the findings to prior arithmetic and attention-sink research.

P1.justification: The seven-section main structure and much existing prose remain. Local revisions qualify the abstract and conclusion, consolidate related-work headings, separate the Results subsection and expand discussion subsections. Appendix A becomes a procedural guide, and an impact statement and conference header are added.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays through new Tables 6–10 and 13–14, uncertainty-formatted summary tables, additional model/universal-head rows and a boxed prompt list. The retained WMDP plots are resized, arranged side by side and renumbered; original appendix tables are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves evidential calibration and reproducibility through the necessity-versus-sufficiency qualification, uncertainty reporting, new robustness controls, stability analyses and concrete implementation settings. These address important interpretive and validation gaps in v1. Numerical reconciliation remains imperfect: Table 3 reports a HumanEval drop of 15.9, whereas Table 13's 68.3-to-51.6 values imply 16.7, and some summary/appendix standard deviations differ. These defects limit precision but do not outweigh the substantial gains.
